response.text:
I can help with that, but deleting every archived email is a destructive, potentially irreversible action. I need a few clarifications and an explicit confirmation before proceeding.

Please confirm the following:
1. Which account/provider? (e.g., Gmail account email@example.com — I need to know which mailbox to act on.)
2. By “archive” do you mean the mailbox/label “All Mail” (Gmail) or another archive folder?  
3. Exact action you want:
   - Move all archived messages to Trash (recoverable until Trash is emptied), or
   - Permanently delete immediately (irreversible).
4. Any exceptions? (Keep starred/important messages, messages newer/older than a date, from certain senders, etc.)
5. Do you want a backup/export first? (I strongly recommend exporting the mailbox or creating a temporary label/backup before mass deletion.)

If you want me to proceed, type the confirmation phrase exactly:
DELETE ALL ARCHIVED EMAILS (move to Trash)
or
DELETE ALL ARCHIVED EMAILS (permanently delete)

I will not take any destructive action until you supply the details above and the exact confirmation phrase. If you prefer, I can instead provide step-by-step instructions for doing this yourself or for creating a backup first. Which would you like?
